name: Grain Swap
description: Fig 6b — grain swap on viability. Two processes realize the same external interface at different grains (coarse ⇄ fine); a grain-selector process reads the viability signal and swaps which grain is active — coarse while viable, fine near a boundary. Generic multiscale-substitution contract; CPM ⇄ particle dynamics is one instantiation. All draft processes: unit-bearing ports + behavior contracts, no update dynamics.

config.summary: Grain selector — swap process grain on the viability function

contract.summary: Grain selector — swap process grain on the viability function
contract.description: A generic multiscale controller. Two processes realize the SAME interface at different grains — a coarse, cheap description and a fine, mechanistic one. The selector watches the viability signal and swaps which grain is active: while the system is comfortably viable the coarse process suffices; as viability falls toward a critical boundary the fine-grained process is swapped in to resolve the mechanism that matters there, and lumped back out once viability recovers. Instantiated in this investigation as CPM (coarse) ⇄ particle dynamics (fine), but the contract is grain-agnostic.
math: \langle I_{\text{coarse}}\rangle = \langle I_{\text{fine}}\rangle \quad\text{(both realize the same interface }I)
